'''Alan Gaius Ramsay McIntosh''' (17 January 1942 – 8 August 2016) was an Australian mathematician who dealt with analysis ([[harmonic analysis]], [[partial differential equation]]s). He was a professor at the [[Australian National University]] in Canberra.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://researchers.anu.edu.au/researchers/mcintosh-agr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110416061507/https://researchers.anu.edu.au/researchers/mcintosh-agr|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 April 2011|title=Professor Alan McIntosh|access-date=3 February 2020}}</ref>

McIntosh was born in Sydney, New South Wales on 17 January 1952.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=McIntosh, Alan Gaius Ramsay |url=https://www.eoas.info/biogs/P003298b.htm |access-date=2025-09-11 |website=Encyclopedia of Australian Science and Innovation |language=en-gb}}</ref> He studied at the [[University of New England (Australia)|University of New England]] with a bachelor's degree in 1962 (as a student he also received the University Medal ) and PhD in 1966 with [[Frantisek Wolf]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], for his thesis "Representation of Accretive Bilinear Forms in Hilbert Space by Maximal Accretive Operator ". At Berkeley, he was also a student of [[Tosio Kato]]. As a post-doctoral student, he was at the Institute for Advanced Study and from 1967 he taught at [[Macquarie University]], moving to the Australian National University in 1999.<ref name=":0" /> In 2014 he became emeritus.

McIntosh was involved in solving the [[Calderon conjecture]] in the theory of [[singular integral operator]]s.

In 2002, he solved with [[Pascal Auscher]], [[Michael Lacey (mathematician)|Michael T. Lacey]], [[Philipp Tchamitchian]] and [[Steve Hofmann]] the open [[Kato root problem]] for [[elliptic differential operator]]s.

He also worked on [[singular integral operator]]s, [[boundary value problem]]s of partial differential equations with applications (such as [[scattering theory]] of the [[Maxwell equations]] in irregular areas), [[spectral theory]] and [[functional calculus]] of operators in [[Banach space]]s, analysis with [[Clifford algebra]]s, barriers for the [[heat kernel equation]] and functional calculus for [[elliptic partial differential operator]]s.

In 1986 he became a fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]], whose [[Hannan Medal]] he received in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.science.org.au/opportunities-scientists/recognition/honorific-awards/career-awards/hannan-medal|title=Hannan Medal|access-date=3 February 2020}}</ref> In 2002 he received the [[Moyal Medal]] from Macquarie University.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mq.edu.au/about/about-the-university/faculties-and-departments/faculty-of-science-and-engineering/departments-and-centres/department-of-mathematics-and-statistics/news-and-events/events/events/moyal-medal|title=Moyal Medal|access-date=3 February 2020}}</ref>
